title: Simultaneously Capturing Real-time Images in Two Emission Channels Using a Dual Camera Emission Splitting System: Applications to Cell Adhesion
protocol: Purchase StreamPix 5 Multi-Camera software with SimulPix module or other imaging software capable of collecting and combining images captured by monochrome CCD cameras.
Connect the DC2 Photometrics emission splitter, or similar dual camera emission splitting device, to the microscope.
Insert two monochrome CCD cameras into female C-mount 1 and female C-mount 2.
Use imaging software to display images from both cameras.
Open StreamPix 5 and select "workspace" in the task ribbon.
Open "workspace manager" located at far right of the screen.
Select "new workspace".
Name a camera and follow software prompts to select a grabber from a pre-populated list.
Repeat the process for the second camera workspace, selecting the appropriate grabber matching the camera model.
Load the merged workspace.
Assign cameras from workspace 1 and workspace 2 to the merged workspace in the docking panel on the right-hand side of the viewing screen.
Align cameras in the dual camera emission splitting system using bright field or phase contrast with the calibration grid provided by the manufacturer.
Place the metallic-coated calibration grid on the microscope stage, squaring it.
Bring the grid into focus.
Displace but do not remove the dichroic housing to align camera 1 (bypass camera).
Display the grid without binning and without autoscaling using PlanApo 40X objective or greater.
Focus the image using the focus adjustment dial on C-mount port 1.
Push the dichroic housing into the dual channel acquisition device fully, so that the image is split by the dichroic to both cameras.
Loosen the three 5/64" set screws and rotate the second camera on the female C-mount until the orientation of the grid is identical in both images.
Bring the image from camera 2 into focus using the focus adjustment dial on C-mount port 2.
Finalize alignment using the combined image in the merged workspace of the imaging software.
Adjust the combined image positions using only the R/L knob on the right side of the DC2 until the right/left vertical boundary of the images is precisely aligned.
Use the U/D knob to adjust the up/down alignment of the second image until the horizontal grid bars are properly aligned.
Correct any camera rotation issues by loosening the three 5/64" inch screws for camera 2 and rotating until the displayed image is properly aligned.
Culture BT-20 breast cancer cells in minimum essential medium (MEM) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1% penicillin-streptomycin at 37 °C and 5.0% CO2.
Harvest cancer cells with a dilute trypsin treatment.
Count cells with a hemocytometer.
Wash and suspend cells at 10^7 cells/ml in 0.1% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in DPBS with calcium and magnesium (DPBS+).
Dilute primary antibodies, purified mouse anti-human CD24 and purified rat HECA-452, to a predetermined optimal concentration in 0.1% BSA DPBS+.
Incubate cells for 30 min.
Centrifuge cells at 1,200 rpm to obtain a cell pellet.
Aspirate primary antibody.
Wash cells twice with 0.1% BSA DBPS+.
Dilute secondary antibodies, goat anti-mouse IgG AlexaFluor 568 and goat anti-rat IgM AlexaFluor 488, to a predetermined optimal concentration in 0.1% BSA DPBS+.
Incubate cells for 30 min.
Wash cells twice.
Suspend cells in 0.1% BSA DPBS+ at 106 cells/ml.
Connect tubing to the inlet and outlet ports of the parallel plate flow chamber.
Connect one tube to the reservoir of labeled cells suspended in 0.1% BSA DPBS+.
Connect another tube to the syringe pump.
Attach a vacuum line to the flow chamber.
Position the flow chamber over a 35 mm tissue culture dish containing a monolayer of Chinese hamster ovary cells expressing E-selectin (CHO-E).
Adjust the flow chamber and/or gasket for an adequate vacuum seal.
Withdraw fluid from reservoir, monitoring the flow chamber assembly for proper seal and no visual evidence of air bubble formation.
Place flow chamber assembly on microscope (Leica DMI 6000B).
Power a Leica EL-6000 compact light source or similar device to generate high intensity light and couple it into a light guide.
Pass this light through a combination filter cube, i.e., G/R (green/red) filter cube, to excite fluorophores of a desired color/intensity.
Ensure dichroic housing is in correct operating position (depressed) and is not in bypass mode.
Operate microscope in fluorescence mode and select proper fluorescence filter cube (green/red).
Determine the exposure time and gain in camera 1 (red; 620±60 nm) and camera 2 (green; 535±40 nm).
Depress the dichroic to obtain images in both the red and green emission channels.

Use a flow chamber assay with cells labeled with the red fluorophore only, and obtain an image in the red channel by adjusting the exposure time of camera 1 in "live settings" of the imaging software.
Match the exposure time of camera 2 to the exposure time of camera 1.
Reduce the exposure time in both cameras if bleed-through artifacts are visible in the green channel.
Adjust the gain of camera 1 to improve image visibility in the red channel if necessary.
Repeat steps with cells labeled only with the green fluorophore, defining exposure time for camera 2 to avoid bleed-through artifacts in the red channel.
Retitrate antibodies if bleed-through artifacts cannot be eliminated or if exposure times differ substantially between cameras.
Use imaging software to view images simultaneously captured from two monochrome CCD cameras in the flow chamber experiment.
Merge images collected from both cameras using the SimulPix module of Streampix 5 or an alternative software package.
Use digital correction adjustments in SimulPix or alternative software to spatially align the merged images if necessary.
